title: Cajeta capability vocabulary — v1
description: Canonical capability list referenced by action declarations (action-catalog-v1.json), plugin manifests, and the `settings.plugins-allowed-capabilities` / `settings.capabilities` knobs in cajeta.json. Authoritative C++ source is the `Capability` enum in src/cajeta/buildtool/Sandbox.h. Adding a new capability is a minor-version bump of this document. Removing one is a major-version bump.

deploy-time-enforcement.description: How the capability is enforced when sandboxing is active (Phase 11). `bwrap` for Linux; macOS / Windows currently stub but document the planned shape.

items.description: Action names that include this capability in their default requested set.

filesystem.description: Read or write files inside the project root (and its declared writable paths). Read-only host paths like /usr /lib /etc/alternatives are always available; everything else is denied unless explicitly bound.
filesystem.deploy-time-enforcement: bwrap --bind <project-root> --ro-bind-try /usr /lib /bin /etc/alternatives — outside-root access fails at the sandbox boundary.

process.description: Fork+exec a subprocess. Required for any action that runs the compiler, an installer, or an arbitrary command.
process.deploy-time-enforcement: bwrap inherits the host PID/exec policy; capability is signal-only at the action-validation layer (firstDisallowedCapability rejects pre-invocation).

network.description: Open outbound network connections. Required for HTTP/Git/SFTP repository drivers and cloud uploads. Without this capability the sandbox emits `--unshare-net` so even an action that calls libcurl fails clean.

env.description: Read environment variables. The sandbox `--clearenv`s by default and selectively re-exposes only the variables an action requests (PATH, HOME faked to /tmp, plus action-declared passthrough).
env.deploy-time-enforcement: bwrap --clearenv + --setenv K V per declared passthrough.

notes: Capability semver: adding a capability is a minor bump (consumers must update their allowlists, but existing allowlists keep working — the new capability simply isn't granted). Removing a capability is a major bump.

First-party plugins (cajeta.*) get a wider default allowlist than user plugins; see Plugin.cpp::resolvePlugins. The wider default is hard-coded, not configurable — it's part of the plugin namespace contract.
Capability checks fire twice: at action invocation (firstDisallowedCapability gating the action.run() call) and at sandbox wrap (wrapInSandbox translating the granted set into bwrap argv).
